client_brief:
Dealer-ready roll labels and bay imagery for Apexguard

Our dealer meetings need a reliable label system, not another set of labels assembled one by one. Apexguard has three tiers that should read as one family, and the current stock export must control the product information.

Please quote for these outputs:

Four by six inch box end labels, one label per live SKU in export order, rendered at 300 ppi at trim. Every label binds tier, width, roll length, the six performance parameters, the warranty statement and the dealer price verbatim from the stock export, plus the delivered mark artwork rather than last year's. Accompanied by one single label file per SKU named to the SKU code and identity verified by opening it, and by 300 ppi proofs. Produced by reverse engineering the printer's flat PDF into a live merge template, handed back with the record of how it was derived.

Ten in-house frames shot under two different lighting mixes brought to one neutral, judged as a set rather than one at a time, with clear film still reading as clear and tinted glass still reading as tint. Plus one licensed context frame graded into the same neutral. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions, with a per-frame parameter log, one line per-frame on why it differs from its neighbours, and all reported crop and resize limitations recorded.

Film rolls and hood edge details isolated onto the agreed studio ground for the poster and the social set, cut on the product's own edge with nothing bitten away where roll and rack sit at the same value and nothing of the rack left attached. Isolation route recorded per-frame, because a roll standing clear of the rack and a roll against it cannot be produced the same way.

The warranty and six performance parameters are fixed copy. For the photographs, clear film must remain clear and tinted glass must remain visibly tinted. The roll and rack can be close in value, so please choose the isolation method per image instead of applying one route indiscriminately.

Starting files: master_mark_draft/ (mark_draft_2400.png plus shopcard_photo.jpg); bay_frames/ (10 frames, 4600 x 3070); rolllabel_2025_PRINT.pdf; skus_and_tiers.csv; brand_direction.txt.

The live template, correctly named individual labels and 300 ppi proofs are part of the delivery. Please check identity by opening the per-SKU files, not by assuming their returned order.

This is a fixed-price commission at $6,000-$12,000, with a target of 4 to 6 weeks. The agreed review allowance is direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports, a short production and exceptions note and the normalised data and field-mapping record. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory-catalog, not tuner.', a required 'strong master + sub-brand naming' structure, and an explicit exclusion of 'mascots, vintage badges, heavy gradients.' Co-anchor: the Upwork logo-vectorization and brand-identity-kit brief from a client whose logo existed only as a low-resolution raster and who needed print-ready vector artwork plus print and apparel variations and a colour and type reference. Laundered to the fictional Apexguard Surface Systems; no real company, person, product or trademark appears, the mark is original geometry recovered from the client's own supplied artwork, and no craft-software brand name appears in any task-facing field. The ledger records this slot as previously sitting almost entirely on one authoring surface. LAYOUT-17 restores the commission both clients actually posted: the identity has to be recovered as usable artwork, and the point of recovering it is that a dealer deck, a counter poster, an installer social set and a printed roll label all carry it and all have to agree.

price_band_and_audience: Full vehicle paint protection film installs 1,800 to 6,000 dollars; tint packages 400 to 1,200 dollars; film sold by the roll to installers at 900 to 4,200 dollars a roll. Two audiences: dealer group principals and fixed operations managers, 35 to 55, deciding whether to put Apexguard on their reconditioning line, and independent installer owners, 28 to 50, who buy film by the roll and post their own work. The vehicle owner behind both is 30 to 55 and protecting a 60,000 dollar car. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct artefact is precise and near technical: confident spacing, one restrained accent against a deep neutral, film performance stated as a plain table rather than as a burst, photography that is clean and even rather than dramatic. Push it toward discount tint shop grammar, starbursts, chrome bevels, percentage flashes, three exclamation colours, and a dealer principal reads it as a two hundred dollar tint job and stops believing the ten year warranty printed beside it, which is the exact failure the client describes when they say not factory catalog and not tuner. Push it the other way into moody cinematic car culture and it reads as an enthusiast page rather than a supplier a dealer group can put on its reconditioning line. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,200 to 4,500 dollars fixed, or 50 to 85 dollars an hour across 40 to 60 hours.

assets_supplied.name: master_mark_draft/ (mark_draft_2400.png plus shopcard_photo.jpg)
assets_supplied.kind: The drafted master mark supplied only as a flat 2400 px raster on a light ground, plus a phone photograph of the installer shop card that was printed from an earlier round of the same draft.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'The mark as it was drafted for us, and the card we had printed off it. That is everything we have. No working file.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. The draft carries a hairline keyline around the shield and a narrow counter inside the inner chevron that survive a trace at canvas size and stop being holes at the sizes this mark actually gets used at, and nothing in the traced artwork declares that. The photographed shop card is an earlier revision whose chevron angle and wordmark tracking do not match the 2400 px file, so recovering the mark from whichever source is easier to select produces artwork that will not sit with the rest of the rollout.

assets_supplied.name: bay_frames/ (10 frames, 4600 x 3070)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house photography shot in the company's own install bay: film rolls on the rack, a car mid wrap, hood edge and door shut line close ups, tinted glass, a squeegee pull.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Our own bay, our own camera. Some of it on the Saturday, the rest later that week. It does not hang together.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The bay runs sodium overheads at one end and LED work lamps at the other, and the two sessions were shot under different mixes, so half the range carries a green cast that reads as a film tint difference rather than as a lighting difference. Separately, the matte black film rolls sit on a dark grey steel rack at almost the same value, so an isolation of a roll reports success and quietly takes a bite out of the roll's own edge where the two meet.

assets_supplied.name: rolllabel_2025_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The print shop's flat press PDF of last season's film roll box end label, 4 by 6 inches, one SKU per label, fonts embedded, produced from the company's own system through a full print engine. Carries the tier name, a width and length line, a six row performance block, a warranty statement and a small mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'What the printer sent us last year. Nobody here knows how it was built. Keep it looking exactly like this and put this year's widths and wording through it.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at Apexguard could tell you. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so the tier name, the width line, the performance rows and the warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames to map, and everything has to be driven by ordered offsets inside that one story. And the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording: a longer statement does not spill and does not flag, it simply stops rendering where the frame ends, and every response in the chain still reports success.

assets_supplied.name: skus_and_tiers.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the company's stock system, one row per film roll SKU, with columns for SKU code, tier, width, roll length, the six performance parameters, warranty statement, dealer price and an image column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Straight out of our system. The performance numbers and the warranty wording are ours and we are held to them as written.'
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Fourteen rows for twelve live SKUs: two superseded widths the system still emits, marked only by a withdrawn date column the client never mentions. Tier names carry trailing spaces from the spreadsheet that exported them, the image column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires, and three warranty statements rewritten by the legal reviewer run roughly four times the length of the others.

assets_supplied.name: brand_direction.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page of written direction from the owner, in plain language, with no colour values and no type names.
assets_supplied.visible_description: 'Premium, modern, performance automotive. Minimalist and confident. Not flashy, not factory catalog, not tuner. No mascots, no vintage badges, no heavy gradients.'

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the sizes it is actually used at, on the grounds it is actually used on. The trace is clean and correct at canvas size on white: the shield keyline is a hairline, the inner chevron counter is a hole, the tier lockup's small type is separated. Placed at its true reproduction size on the deck's deep neutral and at box end size on the roll label, the counter closes into a solid, the keyline either disappears or merges with the shield edge, and the tier word thickens into a bar. Nothing in the trace, the artwork or any response reports this, because at the moment of tracing the artwork is genuinely correct. It becomes wrong only in the relationship between this particular drafted geometry, this particular reproduction size and this particular ground, none of which exist as a number anywhere.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot either: a trace that is faithful to the draft is the correct output of the tracing step, and the tool takes no options that would change the result, so there is no first time to get right. Nothing states it, because the brief asks for artwork that holds at the smallest place it is used, which is an ordinary client requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description mentions the keyline or the counter. And the response is not a re-run: the mark has to be re-derived from a differently prepared raster, a minimum size rule has to be written that did not previously exist, and a small size variant has to be designed and then adopted across the label, the social set and the basis page.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mark from a mask prepared differently at the raster stage, since the trace itself has no lever, and judge the result again at true size on the deep neutral rather than at canvas size. Where the geometry still will not hold at label size, author a simplified small size variant, write the minimum size rule and the variant into the mark family basis page, and go back through the label mapping and the social set so both carry the variant they should be carrying rather than the master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A rollout in which the mark is a legible piece of artwork in the deck and a dark blob on every film roll box in every installer shop, delivered to a client whose entire brief was an identity that works on digital channels and on physical packaging.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's label actually exposes, and then whether the merged labels carry what the export says. The label was set as one continuous flowing block, so tier name, width line, performance rows and warranty statement all convert into a single story with no per field frames, and the mapping has to be driven entirely by ordered offsets. The second fact only arrives at trim: the warranty block sits in a fixed measure frame sized to last season's shorter wording, so the three longer statements do not spill, do not reflow and do not raise an overset flag anywhere. The text simply stops at the frame edge, mid sentence, on those three labels, and the merge response, the render response and the label at proof scale all look correct.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before conversion and has no read ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The truncation is worse: a fixed frame that stops rendering produces no error, no warning and no visual alarm at proof scale, so an agent that maps carefully, validates cleanly and renders successfully still ships three wrong labels. It is not a propagation re-run either, because the answer is not to re-merge: it is to decide, with the client, what happens to wording that cannot be shortened inside a frame that cannot be resized.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered label at true trim rather than at proof scale, against its export row, word by word through the warranty statement. Confirm the frame measure from the document rather than from the rendered page, establish which statements exceed it, and escalate in writing before the press file is committed, since the acceptance bar forbids shortening or rewording anything to make it fit. Re-plan the mark binding at the same time if the placement proof from the earlier checkpoint changed which variant the label should carry.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve film roll labels printed and shipped in which three carry a warranty statement that stops mid sentence, sold to installers who resell that warranty to a vehicle owner, with every tool in the chain having reported success and the proof having looked right.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did with the three constructs the rollout depends on: the tier comparison carried in as a real table with per cell strokes, the recovered mark family carried in as inline vector, and the installer social canvases carried in at shapes different from the deck. None of those can be confirmed by any channel other than reading the markup the import returns, and every drop this importer performs comes back as an unqualified success. The multi canvas shape compounds it, because the visual preview resolves only the first canvas, so whatever happened on the poster, the social set and the basis page is reported by the returned markup and by nothing else.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: How this importer normalises a given construct is not documented anywhere the agent can read ahead, is not a parameter, and is not signalled by the response status, so authoring more carefully does not tell you what happened. Nothing states it: the brief asks for live text, a real table and artwork that can be recoloured, which is the client's requirement for a file they can edit, and names no importer and no failure. And the response is not a re-run, because a construct that did not survive has to be re-authored in a different form, and the layout around it changes with it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Parse the returned markup per canvas, not only the first, and check that every photograph resolved to real image data rather than the importer's placeholder, that the mark arrived as path shapes rather than one flattened element, that the comparison arrived as real cells rather than a stack of loose text, that every text element carries the intended face and the intended numeric weight rather than a silent fallback, and that no element resolves past its declared canvas width. Re-author whichever constructs did not survive, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and inspect again rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dealer deck and counter poster handed over as the client's editable file in which the tier comparison is a heap of loose text and the mark family page is empty geometry, discovered by a sales manager in front of a dealer group because the only canvas anyone looked at was the first one.

decision_gates: The surface split: labels to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one record per label, everything else to HTML authoring because it needs several canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which of two supplied mark sources is the current revision, knowing the whole rollout carries whichever one is chosen.
How the mark is named in the selection prompt, since naming the sheet it sits on pulls the mask to the sheet and every downstream step then operates on a rectangle.
Whether the recovered mark holds at true reproduction size on the deep neutral and at label size, and what the minimum size rule should therefore be.
How far to separate the three tier colourways within the hue movement actually available, so the tiers read as a family rather than as three brands.
Which session sets the neutral, and how far to correct the other before the correction itself becomes a visible film tint change.
Isolation route per frame, where a one call knockout is right for a roll standing clear of the rack and returns a bitten edge where roll and rack share value.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's own label story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
